# Copilot Instructions

- **Project**: STM32F103 single-axis FOC demo using HAL-generated init code plus custom BSP for FOC, CAN command control, and AS5600 I2C magnetic encoder feedback.
- **Startup flow**: [Core/Src/main.c](Core/Src/main.c) initializes HAL (GPIO/DMA/I2C1/TIM3 PWM/TIM4 base/TIM2 optional/UART1/CAN), seeds the `FOC motor_foc` struct (supply/limits/pole pairs/dir/PID gains), links timer/sensor/PID structs, starts DWT timing, initializes CAN, blocks until AS5600 reports a valid magnet, waits for a CAN start frame (`StdId` 0x301) before enabling control.
- **Control loop**: TIM4 periodic interrupt sets `TIM4_flag`; the main loop calls `Pidloop()`, `foc_loop()`, and `foc_move()` when the flag is raised. TIM2 logging is present but disabled. Control-target codes are used inconsistently with comments—actual behavior: 0=open-loop voltage (Uq direct), 1=position loop, 2=velocity loop, 3=IMU-driven position surrogate.
- **FOC core**: [BSP/FOC.c](BSP/FOC.c) applies simple SVM-like modulation (`setPhaseVoltage`), normalizes electric angle from pole pairs/dir/zero offset, and writes PWM compare values scaled to ~1800 counts on TIM3 CH2/3/4. `foc_Init` ramps an alignment voltage to find `zero_electric_angle`; avoid skipping if preset is required. Use `Motor_Link*` helpers to copy timer/sensor/PID structs into `FOC` before control.
- **Sensor & timing**: [BSP/AS5600.c](BSP/AS5600.c) reads raw angle via I2C1; [BSP/sensor.c](BSP/sensor.c) unwraps rotations and derives velocity using `DWT_Get_Microsecond` from [BSP/dwt_delay.h](BSP/dwt_delay.h). `DWT_Timer_Init()` must be called before velocity/PID timing; guard against dt >0.5 s is already in `PidCompute`.
- **PID specifics**: [BSP/pid.c](BSP/pid.c) integrates error every call and low-pass filters the derivative (default 20 Hz if unset). `PID_Controller.direction` is multiplied at the end (use -1 when motor dir inverted). There is no anti-windup or output limiting—add locally if needed.
- **CAN protocol**: [BSP/MyCan.c](BSP/MyCan.c) configures filter bank 0 with ID 0x300 mask 0x7E0 (accepts 0x300–0x37F). Handlers: 0x301 sets `can_run_flag=1` (unblocks main); 0x302 triggers `HAL_NVIC_SystemReset`; 0x303 takes a float payload and routes to `Uq`/position/velocity/`imu_data` depending on `control_target`; 0x304 writes `control_target` from `data[0]`; 0x305 is reserved and currently just clears the receive flag. Note `can_rx_flag` is only cleared in the 0x305 branch—if you add new frames, remember to clear it.
- **Conventions**: Prefer edits inside `/* USER CODE BEGIN */` blocks in HAL-generated files. Keep all numerics in floats (no doubles) to match existing structs. Maintain ASCII comments.
- **Build/flash**: Open [MDK-ARM/F103_FOC_TEST01.uvprojx](MDK-ARM/F103_FOC_TEST01.uvprojx) in Keil µVision (target STM32F103C8). Generated CubeMX code paths (MX_*) imply regeneration via CubeMX if pinout changes. SWD + ST-Link assumed; UART1 printf is retargeted in [Core/Src/main.c](Core/Src/main.c) via `fputc`.
- **Debug habits**: Use TIM2 logging (currently disabled) for frequency/angle/Uq prints or pipe telemetry over UART1. Control loop frequency derives from TIM4 period—adjust there, not in the while loop.
- **Extending control**: Use `Motor_SetTarget*` helpers instead of poking PID setpoints directly; ensure `control_target` and PID gains align with desired mode. When adding protocols (e.g., Modbus), hook into the main loop alongside `MyCan_ProcessReceivedMessage()`.
- **Safety**: Alignment applies voltage ramps; ensure load is safe before running `foc_Init`. Voltage limits (`voltage_limit`, `voltage_power_supply`) gate PWM duty—verify before increasing Uq.

Feel free to refine sections that seem incomplete or unclear after you explore more of the board support code.
